source: Cracku (Unacademy) - SSC CGL Tier I 2023 Question Paper Shift 2 (July 14th), memory-based solved question paper with all 100 questions: https://cracku.in/ssc-cgl-tier-1-14th-july-2023-shift-2-question-paper-solved (accessed 2026-08-24). Primary and only complete question-level source found for this specific date+shift (the Adda247/Collegedekho exam-screen export used for Shift 1, ssc_cgl_2023_tier_1_14th-july-2023-shift-2.pdf, no longer exists on the CDN - HTTP NoSuchKey; the Adda247 'Memory Based Paper Based on 14-Jul-2023 Exam' PDF is a day-level compilation whose questions do NOT match this shift).

corroborating_sources.name: CareerPower (Adda247 network) - SSC CGL Shift 2 Exam Analysis 2023, 14 July (published the day of the exam)
corroborating_sources.note: Confirms this date+shift was conducted and states the Tier I pattern used: 4 sections (GI&R 25, GA 25, Quant 25, English 25) = 100 questions, 200 marks, 60 minutes, -0.50 negative marking. Section-wise good attempts (Reasoning 18-20, GA 17-19, Quant 19-21, English 17-19) are consistent with a standard CGL 2023 shift.

corroborating_sources.name: HelloScholar - SSC CGL Exam Analysis 14 July 2023 All Shifts (published 14 July 2023)
corroborating_sources.note: Independent same-day publication listing 4 shift timings for 14 July 2023 (Shift 1 09:00-10:00, Shift 2 11:45-12:45, Shift 3 14:30-15:30, Shift 4 17:15-18:15), corroborating that a Shift 2 took place at 11:45 AM. Page body no longer retrievable via this environment's fetcher (returns 404); shift-timing detail corroborated from the indexed search snippet. Topic list in that snippet (Article 143, UCC, Nobel Prize, TAPI Basin) is from the all-shifts compilation, not shift-specific.

notes: AUTHENTICITY: SSC does not publish CGL Tier I question papers. No exam-screen capture (SSC CBE export) could be located for this specific shift, so this file is based on the single complete independent faculty reconstruction (Cracku, accessed 2026-08-24); date/shift/pattern are independently corroborated as listed in corroborating_sources. The paper should therefore be treated as a faithful memory-based record, NOT as an official SSC document. SECTION ORDER: General Intelligence and Reasoning (Q1-25), General Awareness (Q26-50), Quantitative Aptitude (Q51-75), English Comprehension (Q76-100); global numbering follows that order (consistent with the screen layout of the Shift-1 exam export and with the corroborating pattern table). FIGURES: Q2, Q3, Q7, Q10, Q17, Q23 are non-verbal items and Q55, Q65 are pie-chart items; the source renders them as images not recoverable in this environment, so the question stems are preserved as text and the figures/options are marked [figure - not recoverable]. MATHEMATICAL FORMULAE were typeset in LaTeX in the source and are transcribed here as plain text (e.g. Q54, Q56, Q59, Q63, Q64, Q67, Q72, Q73). KNOWN SOURCE ARTIFACTS are flagged per-question in answer_note (e.g. Q42 option A 'Baikal rocks' is likely a corruption in the source; Q27 option D '9rd' is a deliberate distractor preserved verbatim). ANSWERS: The official SSC answer key for this exam (tentative key uploaded 01-Aug-2023 per notice Write_Up_Tentative_AnswerKey_T1_CGLE_2023_01082023) is only downloadable by candidates logged into ssc.gov.in/ssc.nic.in, and Cracku's faculty solutions on this page are login-gated; no accessible authoritative per-question answer source was available in this environment. Per project answer policy, correct_answer is null for all questions and nothing has been filled in by inference.

(P) Entertainment may be principally found in the centre pages of the newspaper in some of the feature articles and in some local news stories.
(Q) The principal aim of the short news report on the front pages is to inform.
(R) Most newspapers are published daily, and the news reporters must make sure that they have up-to-the minute news.
(S) In their news reports they will aim to create a sense of immediacy, to convey the impression that they have ‘rushed’ the news to the reader and ‘that the information contained is the very latest.’
(S6) Reporters also wish to create a sense of authenticity, that is, that their news is accurate and genuine.
